result.summary:
Independently re-validated TEST-DESIGNER's Step 4 regression test at test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:1375 (commit 7640aedc). Did NOT accept the reported fail-then-pass proof on the strength of the report -- re-applied the same mutant myself, in place (per WF-03's documented fallback: this checkout's git-worktree technique is known to run stale beams, per the docs/anti-patterns.md entry from commit 86f08ad8, so in-place mutation + verified revert is the correct technique here, not a shortcut).

MUTANT APPLIED (mine, not copied): reverted line 1414 from `refute final == baseline` to `assert final == baseline` (the pre-ISS-0881-fix platform-wide equality shape). Ran `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:1375` myself. Real quoted output:
```
  1) test ISS-0881 regression: scoped leak checks tolerate a concurrent partition's unrelated schema churn an unrelated sandbox_% schema created during the baseline-to-final window does not fail the scoped no-leak check (Letflow.SandboxPoolTest)
     test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:1375
     Assertion with == failed
     code:  assert final == baseline
     left:  MapSet.new(["sandbox_noise_test_2"])
     right: MapSet.new([])
     stacktrace:
       test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:1414: (test)

Result: 0/1 passed, 23 excluded
Failed: 1 test
```
This independently reproduces the exact failure signature TEST-DESIGNER reported (same assertion, same left/right MapSet shapes).

REVERT: restored `refute final == baseline` via direct edit. Ran `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` -- output was EMPTY (confirmed clean, matches committed tree). Re-ran `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:1375` myself. Real quoted output:
```
Finished in 3.2 seconds (0.00s async, 3.2s sync)
Result: 1 passed, 23 excluded
```
Both halves of the proof reproduced with my own real output, not copied from step-04's summary. Ran `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` again afterward -- still empty.

ON_EXIT CLEANUP: read the test body directly. Two on_exit callbacks are registered, both BEFORE any assertion that could fail, so ExUnit's on_exit stack runs both unconditionally regardless of test outcome: (1) line 1377, `on_exit(fn -> drop_sandbox_schemas_created_since!(baseline) end)` -- the file's existing best-effort sweep for anything the pool itself leaked; (2) line 1399, `on_exit(fn -> drop_schema!(noise_schema) end)` -- registered immediately after `CREATE SCHEMA` and before any assertion, so the injected noise schema is dropped unconditionally, independent of whether the sweep in (1) also happens to catch it (it wouldn't, since noise_schema is outside the pool's own `baseline`-to-pool-activity diff only incidentally -- see design rationale in the test's own comment at line ~1394-1396). Confirmed this is not conditional on test success.

ISOLATION / SELF-SUFFICIENCY: the test captures its own `baseline` via `sandbox_schema_names()` at its own start, uses a uniquely-named pool via `start_pool!/1` (never the shared singleton), and the noise schema name is minted with `System.unique_integer/1` -- no dependency on another test having run first, no shared mutable fixture, no reliance on execution order. Module is `async: false` (whole-file convention, documented in the moduledoc, for the pre-existing Sandbox `:auto`-mode reason), so it cannot race a concurrently-running test in this same suite process either. Ran the full file (`mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs`) after reverting the mutant: `Finished in 56.3 seconds ... Result: 24 passed` -- confirms this new test coexists cleanly with the other 23 in the file and introduced no ordering dependency or leak.

CORRESPONDENCE TO ISS-0881: read docs/issues/ISS-0881.yaml. The issue is exactly what this test targets -- a platform-wide/cross-partition-visible assertion (`refute MapSet.member?(final, o_schema)` style checks, and by extension any bare `final == baseline`) failing under contention from schema churn the test's own pool didn't create. The new test's mechanism (inject an unrelated sandbox_% schema during the baseline-to-final window, assert the SCOPED check tolerates it) is a faithful deterministic simulation of the diagnosed race, not a reimplementation of SandboxPool's logic -- it exercises the real `SandboxPool.claim/2` and `release/2` and the real `sandbox_schema_names/0` helper shared by every other leak check in this file.

No coverage or isolation gaps found. A broader `mix test` full-suite sanity run beyond this file is not warranted before Step 5: ISS-0881's own diagnosis (step-01 handoff) states the defect requires genuine cross-OS-process full-suite contention that a live rig could not reliably reproduce even at 18 iterations, so a single-process full `mix test` run would not exercise the failure mode either way and would only cost time; the full sandbox_pool_test.exs file run (24 passed, quoted above) is the correct-sized sanity check for a change scoped entirely to that one file.
